summary: Touchscreen firmware update corrupts HID descriptor and blocks Autopilot provisioning on select convertible laptops
description:
Issue summary: After applying vendor touchscreen firmware v2.1.4 to a batch of convertible laptops in the staging provisioning lab, devices fail Autopilot provisioning during OOBE. The Windows provisioning flow stalls at the driver-init step and the provisioning agent reports 'device driver enumeration failed: HID descriptor invalid'.

Impact: Blocks device provisioning for ~12 new devices in the staging batch. Affected units cannot complete Autopilot enrollment which prevents MDM provisioning and corporate image application. Potential to block new hires if this reaches the depot.

Environment: Staging provisioning lab (staging-us-west). Devices are imaged with Redwood corporate reference image (win11-corp-2026.02). Touchscreen firmware applied via vendor FWTool v3.2.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Apply corporate image win11-corp-2026.02 to a target convertible (observed on Lenovo X13 Yoga Gen 3 and Dell 7320 Detachable).
2) Run vendor FWTool to update touchscreen firmware to v2.1.4 (automated step in depot flashing SOP).
3) Boot to OOBE and proceed to network + Autopilot enrollment stage.
4) Observe provisioning agent logs; after driver install stage the device stalls and never reaches the MDM enrollment prompt.

Observed behavior:
- Provisioning agent logs: "ERROR: HID descriptor invalid, endpoint count mismatch"
- Device shows no usable touchscreen in Device Manager (HID-compliant touch not enumerated).
- Autopilot fails with timeout waiting for drivers and reports "driver-install-timeout" in provisioning-agent logs.
- Dell/Lenovo vendor diagnostic tools show malformed HID descriptor when queried over USB-HID interface.

Expected behavior:
- Firmware update should leave HID descriptor compliant and allow OS to enumerate touch device. Autopilot should complete and enroll device into Intune.

Initial logs and evidence:
- Provisioning agent archive: s3://redwood-support/provisioning/INT-860321/agent-archive-2026-03-05.zip
- Windows setupact.log and setupapi.dev.log snippets attached in provisioning archive.
- USBPcap trace extracted from a failing Lenovo X13 Yoga: s3://redwood-support/provisioning/INT-860321/usbtrace-2026-03-06.pcapng
- Vendor firmware package and update manifest: vendor_fw_2.1.4/manifest.json (checksum mismatch on one descriptor blob).

Temporary workaround:
- Re-flash touchscreen firmware back to v2.0.9 (previous known-good) using vendor FWTool -- that allows Autopilot to proceed.
- For already-returned devices in the same batch, reimage + downgrade touchscreen firmware before sending to the employee.

Notes on scope:
- Not all models are affected; desktops and non-convertible laptops were not demonstrating this failure.
- We saw ~12 failing units in the March 4–6 depot batch out of ~80 units updated (failure rate ~15%).
investigation_notes: 03-05: Maya validated reproducible failure in staging with Lenovo X13 Yoga using corporate image and vendor FWTool v3.2.
03-06: Captured USB HID trace; HID descriptor blob in firmware v2.1.4 contains wrong report descriptor length field (0x7A vs expected 0x4A).
03-07: Vendor engaged (Vendor Support Case VND-99871). Vendor acknowledged potential build artifact and provided a patched firmware candidate v2.1.5-rc1 for validation.
03-08: Validated downgrade to v2.0.9 resolves enumeration and Autopilot completes end-to-end.
03-10: Confirmed failure reproduction on Dell Latitude 7320 Detachable; failure pattern identical (report descriptor length mismatch).
03-12: Cross-checked imaging pipeline: no changes to driver packages or provisioning agent between 2026-02 and 2026-03 batches. Suspect firmware as root cause.
03-13: Drafted SIG checklist to prevent auto-apply of unverified firmware in depot flashing SOP until vendor patch verified.
Current hypothesis: firmware build on vendor side accidentally included host-specific HID padding bytes leading to malformed descriptor length that the Windows HID parser rejects during enumeration.
comments: Maya Chen (Reporter) - 2026-03-05: Filed after first batch failures. Attached setup logs and USB trace. Requesting hold on further FW pushes to depot.
Diego Ramos (Assignee) - 2026-03-06: Confirmed repro in lab. Reverted two devices to v2.0.9 and they completed Autopilot successfully. Opening vendor case.
IT Depot Lead - 2026-03-07: Paused automated firmware pushes from vendor pipeline. Manually set depot to skip v2.1.4 images.
Vendor Support (VND) - 2026-03-08: Acknowledged issue and provided v2.1.5-rc1 build for internal validation. Notified we'll test on 5 units.
Diego Ramos - 2026-03-11: Validated v2.1.5-rc1 on 5 test units (2 Lenovo, 3 Dell). All sampled units enumerate correctly. Requesting guidance from Release PM to approve rollout.
Release PM (Asha Patel) - 2026-03-12: Requested regression matrix and sign-off from Security/Driver team. Scheduled canary rollout of v2.1.5-rc1 to 10 units in staging on 2026-03-16.
SRE (Jordan Kim) - 2026-03-13: Added provisioning metric alert to detect driver-enumeration timeouts exceeding 30s (alert: PROV-HID-ENUM-30s).
resolution_notes: Mitigation in place: depot flashing pipeline paused for vendor v2.1.4. Downgrade to v2.0.9 allowed affected devices to complete Autopilot. Vendor provided v2.1.5-rc1 which passed lab validation on small sample. Plan: canary firmware roll-out to 10 staging units 2026-03-16, monitor PROV-HID-ENUM-30s alert for 48h, then staged rollout across depot. Follow-up: update SOP to require firmware descriptor validation with USBPcap on any new vendor firmware builds.
next_steps: 03-16: Run canary rollout of v2.1.5-rc1 on 10 staging units and monitor for HID enumeration errors.
If canary clean: schedule staged rollout across depot with rollback window and automated downgrade script.
Update depot SOP to include USB descriptor validation step and add firmware version allowlist for automated pushes.
Close Vendor Support Case VND-99871 after final vendor build signed and checksum-proofed.
Create a short KB for depot technicians describing how to detect and downgrade malformed touchscreen firmware during imaging.
